articles.image_title: Migration nach Ceuta: CEUTA, SPAIN - JULY 31: Several migrants are sleeping as best they can, on 31 July, 2026 in Ceuta, Spain. The autonomous city of Ceuta awoke to find that large numbers of people were still entering from Morocco early this morning, following a night in which the influx across the border area had continued unabated. Thousands of migrants have entered the autonomous city today, either by swimming or on foot along the breakwater that separates the autonomous city from Morocco. Police sources state that more than 20,000 people are believed to have entered Spain. (Photo By Jesus Torres/Europa Press via Getty Images)

articles.title: Ceuta und Melilla: Warum gibt es spanische Gebiete in Nordafrika?
articles.teaser: Nur in Ceuta und Melilla hat die EU eine Landgrenze zu einem afrikanischen Staat. Doch der Status der beiden Städte ist umstritten. Was ist die Geschichte der Exklaven?
articles.image_title: Ceuta und Melilla: Dieses am 24. Februar 2024 in Melilla aufgenommene Foto zeigt eine spanische Flagge an einem Zaun in der Nähe eines geschlossenen Grenzübergangs an der Grenze zwischen Marokko (oben) und der spanischen Enklave Melilla in Nordafrika. Am 24. Juni 2022 starben 23 Migranten und Asylsuchende nach einer Massenpanik am Grenzzaun von Melilla, an der marokkanische Beamte und spanische Zivilgardisten beteiligt waren. Ceuta und Melilla, zwei spanische Gebiete an der nordmarokkanischen Küste, sind die einzigen Landgrenzen der Europäischen Union auf dem afrikanischen Kontinent und häufig das Ziel von Migranten, die hoffen, das europäische Festland zu erreichen.

articles.image_title: Nachrichtenpodcast: he uncontrolled influx of people into Ceuta from Morocco continues into the night. Migrants and those floating across the water after crossing the border between Ceuta and Morocco, July 31, 2026, Madrid, Spain: Numerous people continued to enter Ceuta from Morocco unchecked as night fell on Thursday, July 30. From early in the morning, thousands of migrants had entered the autonomous city by swimming and also on foot, skirting the breakwater that separates the autonomous city from Morocco. Border control units in Ceuta have recovered the bodies of 16 people from the water in the last 24 hours, bringing the total to 47 foreigners found dead in Ceuta’s waters while attempting to swim across from Morocco so far this year. JULY 31, 2026 Madri Copyright: xMarcosxMorenox 7696206

articles.image_title: Gerald Knaus: CEUTA, SPAIN - JULY 30: Hundreds of migrants have attempted to swim from Morocco to the Spanish city of Ceuta in North Africa, while the number of arrivals exceeded 1,500 in just over a week, according to local news in Cueta, Spain on July 30, 2026. As Moroccan and Algerian migrants attempted to reach Ceuta by swimming, most were reportedly intercepted by Moroccan patrol boats. Spain's Maritime Rescue Service and the Spanish Red Cross rescued 117 people from the water, while the Civil Guard assisted around 200 others with patrol boats.
